residuals.name: signed-lie
residuals.why: attribution is not trust: the ledger records what a key signed, and a false dead end is evidence attributed to the compromised key, which the charter accepts as the ceiling of what it can do (SEED-NEXT.md §II.5, the compromised-actor consequence)
residuals.inflicts: a false observation in the curation stores under the compromised actor's name
residuals.stands_in_the_way: conclusion-writing is grant-gated to the curator's proposal path (curation.md); a hypothesis needs support from two distinct non-failed contracts and the promotion gate re-judges every citation at the boundary's own position; revocation ends the key's standing and the reconciler surfaces what it signed

residuals.name: self-exhaustion
residuals.why: a reservation inside the class's remaining capacity is exactly what the permission grants, and nothing distinguishes a reservation the actor means to spend from one it means to strand
residuals.inflicts: the class's remaining capacity on its own contract consumed by its own reservation, so a later reserve on that contract refuses exhausted (exit 27) — denial of its own progress, and the class's until the reservation settles or the window closes
residuals.stands_in_the_way: the reservation is attributable and position-stamped; the operator lane closes a reservation whoever reserved it (budgets.md); the capacity is the contract's class, not the organization's

residuals.name: refusal-flooding
residuals.why: every refused push costs the hook a replay from genesis, and a valid credential can push as often as the transport allows
residuals.inflicts: denial of progress at the remote — latency for honest pushers while refusals are processed — never denial of authority: the ref does not move, and the next valid push lands
residuals.stands_in_the_way: the ref stays where it was after every refusal, the hook stays responsive, and revocation ends the credential's transport access in the reference deployment (the ssh forced command)

residuals.name: test-content
residuals.why: the charter names it (SEED-NEXT.md §II.14): ordinary test content outside the protected surface remains in an implementer's write scope
residuals.inflicts: a commit on its own contract branch that weakens or removes a test the verifier will run
residuals.stands_in_the_way: diff-vs-plan review, the receipt's changed-file inventory, and sealed checks the implementer cannot read (sealed-checks.md); the protected surface itself is write-denied

residuals.name: credential-binding
residuals.why: the pusher's identity is the transport's assertion (SEED_PUSHER): in the reference deployment the ssh forced command derives it from the authenticated key, and in the filesystem fixture the harness sets it — forging it is stealing another actor's credential, which §I.2 places outside the adversary
residuals.inflicts: with a stolen credential, that actor's contract branch; nothing on the ledger, whose half is signature-bound and refuses an event the stolen credential's key did not sign
residuals.stands_in_the_way: the transport's authentication, outside Seed; the ledger half's signatures inside it

residuals.name: one-posture
residuals.why: the drill proves the enforced-self-hosted posture, the charter's reference deployment; cooperative mode has no server-side enforcement by declaration (posture.Consequence) and enforced-forge-hosted is Phase 12 item 2's admission service
residuals.inflicts: nothing here: the harness refuses to build a cooperative fixture, so the drill cannot report green for a posture where the invariant does not hold
residuals.stands_in_the_way: the harness's own refusal, pinned; the doctor stating the cooperative consequence in plain words

residuals.name: revocation-reap
residuals.why: revoking the compromised key ends its standing — every later proposal refuses at the push and its contract branch closes — but its open claim stands on the ledger until reaped, and today's reap needs an interrupt answered by silence (maintenance.md), which a revoked holder never produces
residuals.inflicts: the contract it held stays in_progress under a key that can no longer act on it until an operator or the maintenance lane reaps it
residuals.stands_in_the_way: the reap now lands: os-32d06c65 added admit.RevokedHolder as the third reap corroboration and the maintenance pass reaps a revoked holder's open claim with a force packet (so the work is re-offered) and surfaces it as a claim.reap-owed obligation. What this drill still asserts is the revocation's other two consequences, which stand: a revoked key's ledger proposals refuse at the push, and its contract branch closes with its standing
